sources.citation: Pacchiarotti, Sara & Koen Bostoen. 2025. Language divergence and convergence and deep-time population history in the Kwilu-Kasai region. In An archaeology of the Bantu expansion (Routledge). DOI 10.4324/9781032658148-7.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; Mbuun final-vowel-loss examples in (4) with tone marks; cites Mundeke 2011: 29 for labial-velar stops only.

sources.citation: Pacchiarotti, Sara & Koen Bostoen. 2024. Sound change versus lexical change for subgrouping: word-final lenition of Proto-Bantu *ng in West-Coastal Bantu. Language Dynamics and Change. DOI 10.1163/22105832-bja10033.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; Mbuun only as doculect labels (Mayungu B87X, Mwilambongo B87Y).

sources.citation: Pacchiarotti, Sara & Koen Bostoen. 2021. Final vowel loss in Lower Kasai Bantu (DRC) as a contact-induced change. Journal of Language Contact 14: 437-475.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No stress statement. p. 442: final vowel loss in Lower Kasai languages (incl. Mbuun B87) 'is not phonologically and/or prosodically determined or constrained'; p. 443: 'as discussed . Mundeke (2011) for Mbuun B87, if the tone pattern of the reconstruction was either HL or LH, V2 was lost but its tone was preserved and created a contour tone' - i.e. Mbuun is a tone language with contour tones; word stress not mentioned.

sources.citation: Pacchiarotti, Sara, Natalia Chousou-Polydouri & Koen Bostoen. 2019. Untangling the West-Coastal Bantu mess: identification, geography and phylogeny of the Bantu B50-80 languages. Africana Linguistica 25: 155-229. DOI 10.2143/AL.25.0.3287234.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing (classification/phylogeny; Mbuun appears only in tables).

sources.citation: Bostoen, Koen & Léon Mundeke. 2011. The causative/applicative syncretism in Mbuun (Bantu B87, DRC): Semantic split or phonemic merger? Journal of African Languages and Linguistics 32(2): 179-218. DOI 10.1515/JALL.2011.007.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone. Section 2 (p. 181) only: seven vowels i e ɛ a ɔ o u, most roots -CVC-/-CV:C-/-CGVC-, final vowel generally not realized, verb stems max. two syllables; high tones marked with acute in examples but never described. Data = Idiofa-area Mbuun (fn. 3).

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; only a vowel-notation note (i ɪ ɛ a ɔ ʊ u) and a remark that two plant names differ in 'tonalité'.

sources.note: The only full modern grammar; has a phonology chapter (cited for contour tones p. 443 of Pacchiarotti & Bostoen 2021 and labial-velars p. 29) and would be where any accent/stress statement for the Elyob dialect sits. Bostoen (Ghent) was co-promoter and may hold a PDF.
